### 2026-10-26: # Started researching Ideas

**6h**

# Started researching Ideas

So after designing the curtain opener for my week 1 and 2 projects, I figured that it would be good to continue in the same direction, and try to make something else automated. Then I decided, why not make the thing that automated everything.

So I decided to make a SmartHome Dashboard and controller.

## The Plan

I want to use an E-ink display, as they look really fancy, and are meant to be really low power. I'll use some sort of MCU to control it, probably an esp32s3, so it could be used standalone if needed. However, I plan to also include some sort of SBC capable of running something like home assistant.

So my original plan was to make it fully solar powered, but after finding out the battery draw of SBC's, I've come to the annoying conclusion that the solar power will have to be a backup, or at least supplemented with mains. Also would like to make the solar panel track the sun, but unsure if I will have the budget for this.

## My progress
### E-Ink
Have been researching parts that I can use.

Originally wanted to go with this screen:

![10466](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/QXCoV5Opaf2tVWRHLncynf97ZTE9HKDO/9a5ff8f9b38b02ecf266bc8385b4acb0611a2b4038632406cc60892ba8e4a0c6.png)

This looked good, as $26 is manageable, and I also thought that 3 colour would be good - and the size and resolution is really good - 7.5" at 880x528.

But it has a problem. I'm pretty sure that it will have a much slower refresh rate than a standard bw one, and it will draw much more power as it has to cycle the red out.

So currently I don't know what e ink screen I'll get, but I have this one as a backup.

### SBC's

Due to AI, I guess, SBC's are all stupidly expensive. But I ideally want something that can run home assistant, as I don't fancy trying to code my own. Obviously looked at RPis first, but they're too expensive. But the Pi Zero 2 W, looked interesting, as it's meant to be a really cheap, barely SBC board.

but...

![10464](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/QXCoV5Opaf2tVWRHLncynf97ZTE9HKDO/7d56d4bd5d636b8b6f6ef917b21f1a4c58086c17dfed7b83569fa026135c5b70.png)

They're like all out of stock. EVERYWHERE.

So also having heard of Orange Pi being raspberry pi clones, went and looked them up.

![10467](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/QXCoV5Opaf2tVWRHLncynf97ZTE9HKDO/49363ca88d9e39f4f262d1c8176db6c896fcfacd5cbb0ecd1f9aef7c33dda6fd.png)

Yup, you say the price. A whole $91 for something less powerful than my 2nd gen intel CPU. That was surprising. tbh, didn't realise quite how good 2nd gen intel actually still is.

So with pi clones out of the question, I turned to even more pi clones:

le potato...?

![10468](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/QXCoV5Opaf2tVWRHLncynf97ZTE9HKDO/379e9ab98f54000e902d6b62fef677f530e1c18325922cec6352cd169b98a446.png)

only $60 for mediocre performance...

some random SBC some guy on Reddit suggested: Banana M2 Zero (sounds like another rpi clone loll)

![10463](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/QXCoV5Opaf2tVWRHLncynf97ZTE9HKDO/8a8b49be77df8ff74329496de9853cba0068c6ad88aeaacc23b7304522afe383.png)

Only $32 - a bargain!

Then looked at it, with it's 512mb ram, and essentially non existent support, I figured there's an almost certain chance that home assistant won't run on it - especially as it wants I think at least 2gbs of RAM

### Still on SBC's

I spoke to someone I know who knows electronics, and he suggested an older used rpi board. so I looked at it, and I could actually get a raspberry pi 3 B 1gb model...

![10465](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/QXCoV5Opaf2tVWRHLncynf97ZTE9HKDO/335b8bc9b1a87c81cb03910c066f36e9b9cd8d9411af5a6b024f3e34997c3f1d.png)

for about £20 - a bargain!

Even better, on CEX, with a 5 year warranty:

![10469](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/QXCoV5Opaf2tVWRHLncynf97ZTE9HKDO/073a806276afcd24196bdf792cea36a7e4508da310038be9e2143dc455b054e8.png)

It's only £22 - that's like $30! ($33 with shipping)

No but seriously, I think it should be pretty decent, as whilst is does only have 1gb of ram, the home assistant docs do list it as supported.

So that's where I'm at now. Spending definitely too much time looking up parts options. Have looked up others, but will do in another journal if I have time, as this is getting long. (eg like solar panels, power outputs etc)

## tl;dr

Spent too long looking up parts, mostly to find I don't actually want to use them.

### 2026-10-27: # More Research

# More Research

## A great find

So yesterday, when I looked at SBC's, I decided to go for the Pi3 B (1gb). And that was £22 on CEX. It has since dropped to £20!

But anyway, I have also realised that there is a Pi5 4gb in the shop, but it seems very overpriced, for an interesting price to performance ($151 in shop?? for 4gb?), and I figured I might as well make the project entirely fit in the. $100. and £20, so like $31 with shipping, is a low enough percentage it makes sense. (Though somehow the B+ model has gone up from £28 to £35??)

![10497](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/QXCoV5Opaf2tVWRHLncynf97ZTE9HKDO/9bb5d18578bdda05d8bfb1a848af60440ad61300443e62fc52c929898710fde3.png)

Also did copious amounts of research into whether Home Assistant would actually work on the Pi3. From what I can tell, older versions are definitely supported, newer ones are a bit flaky. But either way, it can run the 64 but version (or not, as community threads seem to say that 64 but is patchy, so may end up on 32), but probably with minimal add-ons.

Spent wayy too much time looking.

![10498](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/QXCoV5Opaf2tVWRHLncynf97ZTE9HKDO/f07364f1d83d873f089d3236f087c81bd459ac6ad573c162659f7d3bdcfdbd6e.png)

But there are GitHub Home Assistant images released for the Pi3. So it should work.
